subject: Evaluation acceptance timeline & SLO rebate structure — Acme POC
messages:
From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acme.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>, procure-acme@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick: POC timeline and SLO-linked commercial ask

Hannah — thanks for the call today. Ben and I talked through next steps internally. High level asks: a 6-week evaluation with 3 milestones (technical validation, quality gate, production readiness) and a proposal that ties a small rebate/credit to latency SLOs during the ramp. Procurement will need clear acceptance criteria for each milestone plus a short SOW and draft contract terms.

Can the Redwood team propose a MAP and an SLA credit table (examples of % credits if p95 > X ms) we can take to procurement this week? We want to confirm pricing at the start but are open to adjusting discounts as long as there are clear ramp commitments from Acme.

Thanks,
Alice Zhao
Head of ML Platforms — Acme Systems

---
Attachment: high-level-acme-requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acme.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: POC timeline and SLO-linked commercial ask

Alice — appreciate the clarity and the list. We can turn around a MAP draft and an SLA rebate table by Thursday EOD PST. Proposed high-level approach:

- 6-week POC split into three two-week milestones (env/setup & baseline, eval/rerun w/ production prompts, ramp to steady-state).
- Define hard acceptance criteria per milestone (latency p95, functional pass rate on your eval set, and max error budget).
- Commercial tie: a capped monthly credit schedule tied to p95 latency and error budget breaches during the ramp window. Credits are additive but capped at X% of that month’s invoice.

Quick question for procurement: do you need the rebate to be time-limited to the POC only, or carry as a temporary credit during first 3 months of production? We can model both options.

I'll attach our draft MAP and SLA table. Monica, Rishi — looping you in for pricing and SLO feasibility.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: POC timeline and SLO-linked commercial ask

Hannah — drafting pricing options now. Two quick commercial levers we can offer to speed close: a) a time-limited onboarding discount if Acme signs an initial 12-month committed capacity after successful POC; or b) a graded discount that grows with committed throughput (e.g., 10% at 25k tokens/day, 15% at 50k tokens/day).

On rebates: prefer a simple SLO credit cap (example below) to avoid complex invoicing:
- If p95 latency < 250 ms: no credit.
- p95 between 250–350 ms: 5% credit up to cap.
- p95 between 350–500 ms: 10% credit.
- p95 > 500 ms or systemic errors: 20% credit (investigate + remediation SLA).

I’ll populate numbers and show impact on unit economics. Rishi — confirm whether 250 ms p95 is realistic for their expected prompt mix (they mentioned long-context summaries).

— Monica
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: POC timeline and SLO-linked commercial ask

Monica — for Acme's stated workload (avg prompt length ~750 tokens, peaks up to 8k tokens), 250 ms p95 is optimistic on most GPUs unless we Q8 quantize and enforce short tail batching. Realistic targets:
- Target baseline: p95 ~= 350 ms with default config.
- Optimized config (aggressive batching + quantization + KV cache): p95 ~= 220–300 ms for short sessions; long-context paths will hit 450–700 ms.

Recommendations: define two SLO buckets in the MAP:
1) Interactive SLO (short prompts < 1k tokens): p95 target 300 ms; credits apply if > 300 ms.
2) Long-context SLO (>= 1k tokens): p95 target 600 ms; credits apply if > 600 ms.

Also propose a small grace period during the first two weeks of ramp while we tune the runtime and cache warm-up. Credits during the grace period should be reduced by 50%.

I’ll add a feasibility note to the MAP draft.

— Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acme.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>, procure-acme@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-10T09:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: POC timeline and SLO-linked commercial ask

Thanks, team — the two-bucket SLO approach makes sense to us. Procurement asked for two specific items before we share with legal: 1) a spelled-out credit table by bucket and month (including cap on credits during the POC); 2) an explicit mutual action plan with dates, owners, and acceptance tests.

We are ok with a 50% reduced credit during the first two weeks of ramp. For production carry-forward, our execs prefer credits be available for the first 90 days of production if Acme commits to a 12-month reserved capacity. That reservation would trigger a 12% onboarding discount.

Can you send a firm MAP + SLO-credit table that includes the reserved-capacity discount scenario?

Best,
Alice

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acme.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Final MAP + SLO-credit proposal (attached) — next steps

Alice / Ben / procurement — please find attached our formal MAP (Acme_MAP_v2.pdf) and a consolidated SLO-credit table (SLA_proposal_table.xlsx). Summary of the proposed commercial linkage and next steps: 

- POC: 6 weeks, three milestones with owners and acceptance criteria included in MAP_v2. First two weeks: environment onboarding + baseline tests; weeks 3–4: quality evals on your prompt set; weeks 5–6: ramp to agreed throughput.
- SLO buckets:
  • Interactive (<1k tokens): target p95 300 ms; credit tiers 0% / 5% / 10% / 20% depending on bands; 50% reduced credit during first 2 weeks.
  • Long-context (>=1k tokens): target p95 600 ms; similar tiered credits and grace reduction.
- Production carry-forward: if Acme signs a 12-month reserved capacity agreement within 30 days of POC completion, Redwood will apply a 12% onboarding discount and make SLO credits available for first 90 days of production (same credit table, uncapped but aggregated cap = 20% of month invoice).
- Pricing and ramp: commercial options included (committed throughput tiers that unlock incremental discounts). Monica attached modeled impact.

Next steps:
1) Review MAP_v2 and SLA spreadsheet (Drive link above).
2) If OK, procurement/Legal to confirm redlines — we can take redlines via DocuSign link provided.
3) Kickoff call to review acceptance tests and monitoring hooks (propose 11/19 10:00 PT).

If anything is missing for procurement, call it out and we’ll update the MAP quickly. Thanks for the productive collaboration — Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0137
